name: Schneider Electric
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Schneider Electric shares the global #1 in data-center physical infrastructure with Vertiv (Dell'Oro has them ~0.1 point apart) and is the clearest practitioner of reference-design-led selling — co-authored grid-to-chip blueprints with NVIDIA from GB200 through Vera Rubin and gigawatt-scale AI factories — while H1 2026 delivered record results (revenue €21.2B, +14% organic; adjusted EBITA +22% organic) on triple-digit data-center demand growth, prompting a raised full-year outlook. BACKGROUND: Founded 1836; ~160,000 employees; FY2025 revenue €40.2B across Energy Management (~82%) and Industrial Automation. CEO Olivier Blum since November 2024, installed abruptly after the board removed Peter Herweck at the peak of the AI cycle. Liquid cooling via the Motivair acquisition (75% for $850M); >$700M US manufacturing expansion through 2027; software layer spans AVEVA, ETAP, and the pending $3.1B Cognite acquisition.
ecosystemRole: We assess Schneider as the diversified incumbent whose data-center franchise sets the procurement template hyperscalers apply to everyone else: validated reference designs, integrated power-plus-cooling scope, and digital twins embedded in NVIDIA's Omniverse. Basis: the only vendor with co-developed NVIDIA designs spanning power management, liquid-cooling controls (Mission Control-interoperable), and gigawatt AI-factory blueprints; a disclosed $373M supply-capacity agreement with Digital Realty; and Dell'Oro's shared #1. Unlike pure-play Vertiv (~75-80% data-center), Schneider's DC exposure sits inside a €40B portfolio — steadier, but the two-speed structure (triple-digit DC demand versus lagging industrial automation) defines its equity story. For challengers, Schneider is the benchmark for what 'selling the design, not the box' looks like.

productsAndServices.name: Secure power / UPS (Galaxy family, APC)
productsAndServices.description: Galaxy VXL flagship (December 2024): 500-1,250 kW per 3-phase modular frame using 125 kW/3U power modules — 1.25 MW in 1.2 m² (claimed 52% footprint improvement), parallelable to 5 MW, up to 99% efficiency in eConversion mode, touch-safe Live Swap module replacement, IEC 62443-4-2 cybersecurity certification. APC Smart-UPS anchors the single-phase/edge base.
productsAndServices.positioning: Company-claimed 'industry's most compact, high-density power protection'; top-5 UPS oligopoly member (with Vertiv, Eaton, Huawei, ABB holding ~40-42% of data-center UPS).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct plus ~1 million channel partners; EcoStruxure IT monitoring attach.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 800 VDC 'sidecar' power system in development: AC-to-800VDC conversion for racks up to 1.2 MW with modular shelves and integrated energy storage for backup and load smoothing — no commercial date disclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Liquid cooling (Motivair by Schneider Electric)
productsAndServices.description: CDUs from 105 kW to 2.5 MW (NVIDIA-certified; company states its cooling backs 6 of the world's top-10 supercomputers), ChilledDoor rear-door heat exchangers to 75 kW/rack, liquid-to-air HDUs (100 kW in a 600 mm footprint), dynamic cold plates, chillers, and EcoStruxure thermal software. Manufacturing tripled via a new Buffalo NY plant plus Italy and India expansions; 600+ cooling field techs in training.
productsAndServices.positioning: Company claims the 'largest installed base of high-density liquid cooling' and the only silicon-level NVIDIA collaboration among cooling providers — contested ground, with Vertiv assembling equivalent scope and Eaton buying Boyd for $9.5B.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and OEM; acquired 75% for $850M (option on the remaining 25% by 2028).
productsAndServices.roadmap: MCDU-45/55 corridor-installed CDUs ramping production early 2026.

productsAndServices.name: NVIDIA reference designs & AI-factory blueprints (grid to chip)
productsAndServices.description: The design franchise: GB200 NVL72 design (132 kW racks, December 2024), GB300 NVL72 design (142 kW racks, up to 1,152 GPUs per hall, ANSI + IEC variants, September 2025), the industry-first integrated power-management + liquid-cooling controls design interoperable with NVIDIA Mission Control, and gigawatt-scale AI-factory blueprints (March 2026 GTC) with ETAP electrical models and AVEVA software embedded in NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX Blueprint — including Vera Rubin NVL72 (480 VAC, 45°C TCS loop) and tokens-per-MW operating-point optimization.
productsAndServices.positioning: The most complete design-led sales machine among incumbents; conversion to orders is inferred rather than disclosed (no design-linked bookings published), but triple-digit DC demand growth and the $373M Digital Realty agreement are consistent with it working.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Reference designs de-risk engineered project sales across the portfolio.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Omniverse-integrated digital twins position Schneider for simulation-first campus procurement.

productsAndServices.name: Prefab/modular data centers & electrical distribution
productsAndServices.description: EcoStruxure Pod (8-12 rack increments) with a prefabricated modular architecture and an OCP-inspired rack system supporting GB200 NVL72 (June 2025, GTC Paris); micro/row/all-in-one builds; MV/LV switchgear, busway, and panels called out as strong data-center sellers. US expansion: >$700M through 2027 across eight sites (El Paso switchgear, Fairfield OH, Houston, Raleigh, Columbia MO).
productsAndServices.positioning: Prefab strength cited in Q4 2025 systems growth; competes directly with Eaton-Fibrebond and Vertiv OneCore/SmartRun.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Engineered systems projects (34% of FY2025 revenue was Systems).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Energy Management year-end backlog €21.3B (+21%) with the largest increase in North America systems on data-center demand.

productsAndServices.name: Software & grid digital layer (AVEVA, ETAP, Cognite pending, AiDASH)
productsAndServices.description: AVEVA industrial software (ARR +11%), ETAP electrical digital twin (the model layer inside the NVIDIA blueprints), RIB construction software; pending: Cognite ($3.1B, industrial DataOps) and ~90% of AiDASH (~$350M, satellite+AI grid risk) joining the One Digital Grid platform. AlphaStruxure delivers energy-as-a-service microgrids.
productsAndServices.positioning: The software layer differentiates the design-led model — electrical simulation, industrial data, and grid analytics under one roof; no direct equivalent at Vertiv or Eaton.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Subscription/SaaS; 19% of FY2025 revenue was Software & Services.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cognite closes into the AVEVA orbit; agentic-AI operations (NVIDIA Nemotron alarm-management pilots) in testing.

recentDevelopments.read: The onshoring race with Eaton and Vertiv, driven by tariffs and hyperscaler proximity.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Schneider's edge is the design layer, not the hardware layer. Basis: the only incumbent with NVIDIA co-developed designs spanning electrical (ETAP), cooling controls (Mission Control interop), and whole-factory blueprints in Omniverse — a position that pulls its hardware into projects before competitive bidding starts. The caveat: no design-linked order figures are published; conversion is inferred from triple-digit demand growth and the $373M Digital Realty agreement.

(High confidence) We assess the two-speed portfolio is both the stabilizer and the discount. Basis: triple-digit data-center demand against Industrial Automation margins that missed (14.2% FY2025) and European industrial softness; RBC's long-standing valuation bear case (~40% sector premium) prices exactly this — the diversified structure cushions AI-capex shocks better than Vertiv but caps the multiple.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the November 2024 CEO ouster remains an unexplained governance discontinuity, now largely cured by delivery. Basis: the board removed Herweck for undetailed execution 'divergences' days after analysts reiterated targets; under Blum the record is one guidance trim (April 2025), then a beat-and-raise trajectory through H1 2026.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Motivair integration is working but the cooling lead is contestable. Basis: manufacturing tripled and the portfolio filled out within a year of closing — while Vertiv assembled equivalent scope through four smaller deals and Eaton paid $9.5B for Boyd; liquid cooling is now a three-way incumbent fight where 'largest installed base' claims are unverifiable.

(Low confidence) We assess the €207M French antitrust fine (resale price fixing, 2012-2018, decided October 2024) is a contained legacy issue rather than a live commercial risk. Basis: appeal pending at the Paris Court of Appeal; no reported customer or procurement consequences to date.
